choices.feedback: It treats neural adaptations as permanent, irreversible damage, ignoring lifelong neuroplasticity.
Brains are frozen like concrete after trauma and can never recover.

choices.text: Ask what the research actually demonstrates
choices.feedback: fMRI and structural MRI studies show functional networks can recalibrate when safe environments, supportive relationships, and evidence-based therapies are introduced.

definition.responsible_version: Trauma alters how brain networks communicate under threat, but lifelong neuroplasticity allows the nervous system to recalibrate toward safety.

title: Trauma is stored in the body's muscle tissue.

definition.purpose: Practice asking what research actually shows before accepting or rejecting a popular claim.
definition.instruction: Read the claim. Choose how you would respond, then compare with the evidence-based reasoning.
definition.accessibility_alternative: All content is plain text; no timing or drag interactions.
definition.claim: Trauma is stored in the body's muscle tissue.

choices.feedback: Muscles do not possess neural synapses required to encode autobiographical event narratives.
Peripheral muscle tissue stores video-like memory files that must be physically massaged out.

choices.text: Ask what the research actually demonstrates
choices.feedback: Cognitive neuroscience confirms that episodic memories are stored across neocortical-hippocampal networks; the body stores conditioned motor reflexes and autonomic threat biases.

definition.responsible_version: Trauma deeply conditions autonomic responses and muscular tension habits, but autobiographical memory resides in neural networks.

title: Your amygdala is broken or stuck on permanently.

definition.purpose: Practice asking what research actually shows before accepting or rejecting a popular claim.
definition.instruction: Read the claim. Choose how you would respond, then compare with the evidence-based reasoning.
definition.accessibility_alternative: All content is plain text; no timing or drag interactions.
definition.claim: Your amygdala is broken or stuck on permanently.

choices.feedback: The amygdala is not broken—it is performing its evolutionary threat-detection function with exquisite vigilance in a system that perceives ongoing danger.
Trauma physically destroys the amygdala like a burnt fuse.

choices.text: Ask what the research actually demonstrates
choices.feedback: Neuroimaging demonstrates that PTSD involves altered connectivity between the Salience Network and prefrontal executive control networks, not cell death in the amygdala.

definition.responsible_version: In post-traumatic stress, the threat-detection network fires with heightened sensitivity due to altered regulatory communication with the prefrontal cortex.

definition.claim: ACE scores predict your personal health destiny.

choices.feedback: It commits the ecological fallacy by applying a population probability directly to an individual's life, ignoring protective factors.
A high ACE score means your adult physical and psychological health is guaranteed to collapse.

choices.text: Ask what the research actually demonstrates
choices.feedback: Longitudinal developmental research shows that positive childhood experiences, subsequent supportive relationships, and economic stability heavily modify outcomes.

definition.responsible_version: Adverse Childhood Experiences increase statistical risk across populations, but individual outcomes are heavily buffered by protective factors and subsequent support.

definition.claim: Ketamine is a miracle cure that permanently resets the brain.

choices.feedback: Without active psychotherapy and behavioral integration during the temporary neuroplastic window, symptoms frequently return within weeks.
A single ketamine infusion permanently deletes trauma and cures PTSD without any therapy.

choices.text: Ask what the research actually demonstrates
choices.feedback: Randomized clinical trials demonstrate rapid transient antidepressant and anti-PTSD effects, but durable recovery requires structured psychotherapeutic integration.

definition.responsible_version: Ketamine opens a temporary neuroplastic window through BDNF release, providing acute relief that requires psychotherapeutic integration for lasting recovery.

title: You must remember every detail of a trauma to heal.

definition.accessibility_alternative: All content is plain text; no timing or drag interactions.
definition.claim: You must remember every detail of a trauma to heal.

choices.feedback: Demanding complete historical recall ignores that severe stress disrupts hippocampal encoding, often creating permanent, harmless memory gaps.
Unrecovered memories will fester indefinitely until every forgotten second is excavated.

choices.text: Ask what the research actually demonstrates
choices.feedback: Clinical trials of CPT and PE demonstrate significant symptom reduction and functional recovery even in survivors with permanent memory gaps.

definition.responsible_version: Trauma recovery requires calming the threat system and updating meaning, not recovering every missing historical detail.
